name: Postwar and Contemporary Period (1946–2000)
description: Literature written in English between the end of the Second World War and the end of the twentieth century: British (English, Scottish, Welsh), Irish and Northern Irish, and American writing, together with the English-language literatures of Canada, Australia, New Zealand, the Caribbean, Africa and South Asia and their diasporas. The audits of installment 10 treat 1951–2000 as the core of the period and report 1946–1950 separately as the bridge from installment 9.
historical_context: The period runs from post-war reconstruction, the welfare state and the Cold War through decolonisation, the civil-rights and women's movements, mass higher education and the paperback and creative-writing booms, to the end of the Cold War, globalisation and the digital revolution of the 1990s.
literary_characteristics: Late modernism gives way to postmodernism while realism persists; the Movement, the New American Poetry, confessional and Language poetry mark the poetry; the Theatre of the Absurd, kitchen-sink and political theatre transform the stage; genre fiction expands into a mass market; literary theory reshapes criticism; and postcolonial, minority and diasporic writing moves from the margins to the centre.
